India’s 121 Languages

An interactive view of India's major language entries by reported mother-tongue speakers, based on the Census of India 2011.
What are Scheduled and Unscheduled Languages?
Scheduled Languages are the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India. The Eighth Schedule currently contains 22 languages.

When the Constitution came into force in 1950, the Eighth Schedule contained 14 languages (Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu).

Subsequent amendments added Sindhi (1967), Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali (1992), and Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santali (2003), bringing it to the present 22 languages.

Unscheduled Languages are recorded Census mother-tongue entries not included in the Eighth Schedule. “Unscheduled” does not mean unofficial or less important.
What is the source and methodology?
Figures are based on the Census of India 2011, Table C-16: Population by Mother Tongue.

Bubble sizes, rankings, and comparisons use the reported mother-tongue speaker counts from this dataset.
